topics.title: Loose coupling: why components talk through messages

kcs.statement: In a loosely coupled architecture, components communicate through intermediaries such as queues or event buses, so one component can fail, slow down or scale without breaking the others.
A synchronous call makes the caller wait for a response; asynchronous messaging lets the sender continue immediately, which absorbs traffic spikes and isolates failures.

problem_ideas: An order web tier calls the payment service directly; payment goes down for 10 minutes. Predict what customers see, then redesign with a queue.
Classify six architecture sketches as tightly or loosely coupled and name the intermediary in each loosely coupled one.
A Black Friday spike sends 20x normal orders; explain which design keeps accepting orders and why.
Pick the Well-Architected design principle that loose coupling supports from four options.
A video upload site makes users wait while transcoding finishes; identify the synchronous step and propose an asynchronous alternative.
Spot the distractor: 'loose coupling means all components run on one larger EC2 instance' and explain why it is wrong.

depth_threads.title: Back-pressure: how a buffer protects a slow consumer
Microservices and loose coupling in the reliability pillar

lens.reason: Exam questions about SQS, SNS and EventBridge usually begin with 'decouple'; this is the idea behind them.

topics.title: Amazon SQS: a managed message queue

kcs.statement: Amazon SQS is a fully managed message queue: producers send messages, consumers poll for them and delete each message after processing, so a slow or failed consumer does not lose work.

SQS standard queues offer nearly unlimited throughput with at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering; FIFO queues keep first-in-first-out order within each message group and deduplicate repeated sends, but a message whose processing is not finished and deleted in time is delivered again, so consumers must handle retries safely.
An SQS queue buffers traffic spikes between tiers, letting an Auto Scaling group of consumers scale on the number of waiting messages instead of the front end failing.

serves.reason: SQS is the default answer to any 'decouple components / buffer requests' requirement on the exam.

requires.reason: SQS is introduced as the queue that delivers loose coupling; the lesson relies on that idea.

problem_ideas: A bank must process payment instructions in exactly the order received: standard or FIFO queue?

An image-resize app receives 10x uploads at noon; place SQS in the design and say what it protects.
Spot the error: 'SQS pushes each message to every subscriber at once.'

depth_threads.title: Visibility timeout and dead-letter queues
Duplicate delivery and idempotent consumers

lens.reason: SQS appears in almost every CLF-C02 form, usually as the 'decouple' answer.

topics.title: Amazon SNS: publish once, notify many

kcs.statement: Amazon SNS is a publish/subscribe service: a publisher sends one message to a topic and SNS immediately pushes a copy to every subscriber; messages are not kept for later polling.
SNS topic subscribers can be SQS queues, Lambda functions, HTTP/S endpoints, email addresses, SMS phone numbers and mobile push endpoints.
Fan-out pairs one SNS topic with several SQS queues so a single event is processed independently and durably by several services.

serves.reason: SNS is the exam's answer for alerts, notifications and one-to-many delivery.

requires.reason: SNS is presented as the push-based way to decouple publishers from subscribers.
The fan-out KC combines SNS with SQS queues and contrasts push with polling.

problem_ideas: A new order must trigger billing, shipping and analytics independently; sketch the SNS-plus-SQS fan-out.
Send an SMS to an on-call engineer when a server fails: which service and which subscriber type?
A subscriber endpoint is down when SNS publishes; compare what happens with and without an SQS queue subscribed.
Match five subscriber types (email, SQS, Lambda, HTTPS, SMS) to five scenarios.
Spot the distractor: 'SNS stores messages until a consumer polls for them.'

depth_threads.title: Message filtering policies on subscriptions

topics.title: Amazon EventBridge: routing events and schedules

kcs.statement: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus: rules match events from AWS services, your own applications or SaaS partners and route them to targets such as Lambda, SQS or Step Functions.
EventBridge can invoke targets on a schedule (cron or rate expressions), for example running a Lambda function every night at 02:00; it evolved from CloudWatch Events.

serves.reason: EventBridge is the in-scope answer for event routing and scheduled triggers.

requires.reason: Event-bus routing is taught as another decoupling pattern.

problem_ideas: Stop all development EC2 instances every weekday at 19:00: which service triggers the Lambda function?
React whenever any EC2 instance changes to the 'stopped' state: write the rule in plain words.
A SaaS help-desk tool emits ticket events; how do they reach your Lambda function without polling?

depth_threads.title: EventBridge Scheduler vs scheduled rules

lens.reason: Shows up in scheduling and event-routing questions; easily confused with SNS.

topics.title: Step Functions workflows and Amazon MQ brokers

kcs.statement: AWS Step Functions orchestrates multi-step workflows as a visual state machine, with built-in retries, branching, parallel steps and waits, coordinating Lambda functions and other AWS services.
Choose Step Functions when the order and outcome of several steps must be coordinated and tracked; choose a queue when one component only needs to hand work to another.

Amazon MQ is a managed message broker for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ, used when migrating applications that already use open protocols such as AMQP, MQTT or JMS instead of rewriting them for SQS and SNS.

serves.reason: Step Functions is in scope as the workflow-orchestration answer; MQ is its common migration distractor.

requires.reason: Both KCs contrast workflows and brokers with the SQS queue.

problem_ideas: A loan approval needs credit check, fraud check in parallel, then a human approval wait: which service coordinates it?

topics.title: Amazon SES: sending email at scale

kcs.statement: Amazon SES sends transactional, marketing and bulk email at scale (and can receive email), with deliverability features such as DKIM signing and sender-reputation tracking.
For customised email to customers, such as HTML receipts or newsletters, choose SES; for simple alert notifications to subscribed endpoints, including email, choose SNS.

serves.reason: SES is a named in-scope business application service for sending email.

requires.reason: The second KC distinguishes SES from SNS email notifications.

topics.title: Choosing a messaging or notification service

kcs.statement: Use SQS to queue work for competing consumers that pull it when they are ready; use SNS to push a notification to multiple subscribers at the same moment.
Routing events from many AWS services or SaaS apps with filtering rules points to EventBridge; coordinating an ordered multi-step process with retries points to Step Functions.
A CloudWatch alarm notifies operators by publishing to an SNS topic, while customer-facing email at scale is sent with SES.

topics.title: Amazon Kinesis: real-time streaming data

kcs.statement: Amazon Kinesis collects and processes streaming data such as clickstreams, IoT telemetry and application logs in real time, making records available to consumers within about a second.

Kinesis Data Streams keeps ordered records for custom consumer applications to read and replay; Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) delivers a stream into destinations such as S3, Redshift or OpenSearch with no code.
With Kinesis several consumers can read the same records and replay them within the retention window, whereas an SQS message is deleted once one consumer processes it.

serves.reason: Kinesis is the in-scope answer for real-time streaming ingestion.

problem_ideas: A game sends 50,000 player events per second for a live leaderboard: Kinesis or SQS?
Stream web logs straight into S3 every minute with no code: which Kinesis option?

topics.title: Athena and Glue: querying a data lake in S3

kcs.statement: Amazon Athena runs standard SQL queries directly on data stored in S3, with no servers to manage, and charges by the amount of data each query scans.
AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service: crawlers discover data and record its schema in the Glue Data Catalog, and Glue jobs extract, transform and load data between stores.
A data lake keeps raw data of any format centrally in S3; Glue catalogues it and Athena queries it in place without loading it into a database.

serves.reason: Athena and Glue are named in-scope analytics services, tested as 'query S3 with SQL' and 'ETL'.

problem_ideas: Analysts want to run SQL on 3 years of CSV logs in S3 once a month without a database: which service?

Spot the distractor: 'Glue is a dashboard tool for business users.'

topics.title: Redshift and EMR: warehousing and big data

kcs.statement: Amazon Redshift is a petabyte-scale, columnar data warehouse for fast SQL analytics on large volumes of structured data.
Amazon EMR runs managed big data frameworks such as Apache Spark, Hadoop and Hive on clusters of EC2 instances (or serverless) to process very large datasets.
RDS and Aurora serve transactional (OLTP) workloads with many small reads and writes; Redshift serves analytical (OLAP) queries that aggregate large historical datasets.

serves.reason: Redshift and EMR are in-scope analytics services and frequent distractors for each other and for RDS.

topics.title: QuickSight dashboards and OpenSearch search

kcs.statement: Amazon QuickSight (Quick Sight in the Amazon Quick suite) is a serverless business intelligence service for interactive dashboards and visualisations built from sources such as Athena, Redshift and S3.
Amazon OpenSearch Service runs managed OpenSearch clusters for full-text search and log analytics with near-real-time querying.

topics.title: Choosing an analytics service for a requirement

kcs.statement: Ad hoc SQL on files already in S3 points to Athena; repeated complex SQL over large structured history points to Redshift; custom Spark or Hadoop processing points to EMR.
Real-time ingestion points to Kinesis, cataloguing and transforming data to Glue, dashboards for business users to QuickSight, and search or log exploration to OpenSearch.
A requirement for transactions or millisecond key lookups points to RDS or DynamoDB, not to an analytics service.

serves.reason: Task 3.7 tests picking the right analytics service from a requirement and ruling out neighbours.

requires.reason: The selection rules include Athena and Glue.

topics.title: Managed AI services for language and speech

kcs.statement: AWS managed AI services expose pre-trained models through simple APIs, so you can add vision, speech or language features without ML expertise or training your own model.
Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text (call transcripts, subtitles); Amazon Polly converts text to lifelike speech.
Amazon Comprehend uses natural language processing to find sentiment, key phrases, entities and language in text; Amazon Translate translates text between languages.
Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots and voice bots with speech recognition and natural-language understanding, the technology behind Alexa.

serves.reason: Task 3.7 tests matching AI services to tasks; language and speech services are the most frequent ones.

problem_ideas: A call centre wants text transcripts of every call and the customer's mood in each: name the two services in order.
An e-learning site needs audio narration of 500 articles: which service?

topics.title: Rekognition, Textract, Kendra and Personalize

kcs.statement: Amazon Rekognition analyses images and video to detect objects, people, text and unsafe content, and to compare faces.
Amazon Textract extracts printed and handwritten text, forms and tables from scanned documents; Comprehend can then analyse the meaning of that text.
Amazon Kendra is ML-powered intelligent search over an organisation's documents; Amazon Personalize generates real-time recommendations from user behaviour.

serves.reason: Vision, document and recommendation services are standard AI service-matching items.

topics.title: Amazon SageMaker AI: building your own models

kcs.statement: Amazon SageMaker AI is a fully managed platform for data scientists to build, train and deploy custom machine learning models at scale.
Choose SageMaker AI when you need a custom model trained on your own data for a unique problem; choose a managed AI service when a pre-trained API already does the task.

topics.title: Generative AI on AWS: Amazon Q and Bedrock

kcs.statement: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed, serverless service that gives API access to foundation models from Amazon and third-party providers to build generative AI applications without managing infrastructure.
Amazon Q is a generative AI assistant: Amazon Q Business answers questions and creates content from a company's own data, and Amazon Q Developer helps write code and work with AWS resources.
To embed a foundation model in your own application use Bedrock; to give employees or developers a ready-made AI assistant use Amazon Q; to train your own model use SageMaker AI.

serves.reason: Amazon Q is in the stage's provides and appears in current AI/ML service-matching questions.

requires.reason: The choice KC contrasts Bedrock and Q with SageMaker AI.

topics.title: Database migration: DMS and the Schema Conversion Tool

kcs.statement: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) migrates databases to AWS while the source stays fully operational, and can continuously replicate changes to keep downtime minimal.
A homogeneous migration (for example Oracle to Oracle on RDS) needs only DMS; a heterogeneous migration (for example Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL) also needs the schema converted first.
The AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) converts a source database's schema and code, such as stored procedures, to a different target engine and flags what it cannot convert automatically.

serves.reason: Task 3.4 names database migration; DMS and SCT are the in-scope answers.

topics.title: Planning and rehosting: Discovery, Evaluator, MGN, Hub

kcs.statement: AWS Application Migration Service (MGN) automates lift-and-shift (rehost) migration by continuously replicating source servers to AWS and launching them as EC2 instances at cutover.
AWS Application Discovery Service collects on-premises server configuration, utilisation and dependency data to plan a migration.
Migration Evaluator builds a data-driven business case by projecting what the current on-premises estate would cost to run on AWS.
AWS Migration Hub is a single place to discover, plan and track the progress of migrations across AWS and partner tools.

serves.reason: These are the in-scope migration services the exam asks you to pick from a migration phase.

requires.reason: MGN is defined as the tool for the rehost strategy among the 7 Rs.

topics.title: AWS Snow Family: moving data offline and at the edge

kcs.statement: AWS Snow Family devices are rugged physical devices that AWS ships to you to move terabytes to petabytes of data offline into S3 when network transfer would be too slow or costly.
Snowball Edge devices also provide edge computing: they can run EC2 instances locally at sites with limited or no connectivity, such as ships, mines or field sites.
AWS guidance: if moving the data over the network would take more than about a week, consider Snow Family devices instead.

serves.reason: Snow Family is the exam answer whenever data volume or connectivity rules out network transfer.

topics.title: DataSync and choosing a data transfer method

kcs.statement: AWS DataSync is an online service that automates and accelerates copying large amounts of data between on-premises storage (NFS, SMB, HDFS, object stores) or other clouds and S3, EFS or FSx, with scheduling and integrity checks.
Network transfer time is roughly data size divided by usable bandwidth: 100 TB over a fully used 1 Gbps link takes about 9 to 10 days.

A one-time or scheduled online bulk copy points to DataSync, ongoing on-premises access to cloud storage to Storage Gateway, too much data for the link to Snow Family, and dedicated private bandwidth to Direct Connect.

serves.reason: Choosing among DataSync, Storage Gateway, Snow and Direct Connect is a standard migration-and-transfer item.

Amazon AppStream 2.0 streams individual desktop applications to a web browser without giving each user a full desktop.
Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser gives workers access to internal websites and SaaS apps through a secure browser session, without data being stored on their devices.
